simulated_boundaries: WMI full and targeted process queries
host_adaptations: Seven inherited WSH COM property-put expressions are adapted to explicit environment setters for Node VM parsing.
Candidate host restores the actual runner runToFile function and simulates results at raw shell.Run; asynchronous process completion writes simulated outputs directly without a nested fake launch.
WMI boundary can return success, absence, matching/mismatched identities, duplicate rows, query errors or partial enumeration errors.
limits: No native Windows, WSH/COM, WMI, Lean/Lake, C#, Wine or CI execution occurred.
All process identities, WMI responses, compiler/audit outcomes, files, receipts, hashes and time are simulated in memory.
Only rows from the initial complete census are revisited. These tests do not assert a global stop-the-world Windows process census or identify unreadable processes as foreign.
Six rounds/64 rows bound targeted worker queries and scheduled sleeps; no hard wall-clock bound is implied for WMI calls.
The current native user failure remains evidence; these mocked cases do not certify the new runner on Windows or promote the mathematical endpoint.
